text: Right, one job each, so nobody can say the crown has favourites. Graham, you hold the Harvest Pile and pay it out fairly. Silke, you bring the tax in honestly. Paddy, you read the I Ching, and the crown pays you five a year so the cards stay kind to all of us. Ten years is a long time, friends, and I mean to see the Wall finished with every one of you still at the table.
Reina appoints Graham Garner banker of the Harvest Pile, Silke Weber tax collector, and Paddy Doyle I Ching reader and keeper of the population counter, at 5 a year from the crown.
Paddy shuffles the I Ching deck; the first card is turned in Year 2.

Storyteller's tip: every work owed at this table is the crown's to pay for, 520 in all. That's six projects (the three palaces, the Wall above Province 1, the Grand Canal in Provinces 1, 5 and 6, and the Province 7 Reservoir), and only one can be built a year, though a project may be built over several years. Tax can be raised only on positive incomes.

Thirty percent, friends: fair on a good year and nothing that pinches. The first thing the crown builds is the Reservoir in Province 7, because a work that feeds people pays for itself. Graham, enjoy the water. Palaces can wait a year, and so can my vanity.
Silke collects the tax at 30%: 18 from each peasant, 54 to the crown.
Reina builds the Province 7 Reservoir on O16 to P17, the crown paying the whole 60. It adds 20 to Graham's harvest from next year. 460 of the works are still owed.
A Customs House, friends, and the coast keeps its books honest. Four to open. Cheap, for the piece that tells you what everyone else is moving.
Silke puts up a Customs House, minimum 4, and keeps the Dragon Jar back.

Thank you, Reina, I'll read the cards straight, whatever they say. I'm putting up a Bamboo Brush, starting at four, same as Silke. I've two of them, so whoever misses this one gets another go next year.
Paddy puts up a Bamboo Brush, minimum 4, and keeps the Wooden Bowl back.

Thank you for the water, Reina. I'll keep the Harvest Pile to the last grain, and you can count it after me any time you like. I'm putting up a Land Deed Scroll at four, same as my neighbours. Land is what this game ends up being about, so it seems fair to sell the paper for it early.
Graham puts up a Land Deed Scroll, minimum 4, and keeps the Vase back.

There are two of each, friends, so let's not bleed the Harvest Pile over the first one. Graham, if you want this Brush badly, take it and I'll have the second next year. Paddy, the same goes for the Deed. If not, I'll go to eight and no further.

There are two of everything here, friends, so there's no need to bleed each other dry. Here's an offer for the whole table: Graham, if you take this Customs House cheap, I'll stay out of it and have the second one next year. Silke, if you let me have this Land Deed, I'll stay out when Graham's second one comes up. If you'd rather bid, that's fine too, but I won't go far.

Each of these pieces has another copy behind it, friends, so I won't bleed the table for any of them. Seven's my limit, no further. Paddy, if you'd rather not race me on the Customs House, take this one cheap and leave me first go at next year's. I'll say the same to Silke about the Brush.

The auctions settle: Paddy buys Silke's Customs House for 8 over Graham's 7; Silke buys Paddy's Bamboo Brush for 8 over Graham's 7; Paddy buys Graham's Land Deed Scroll for 9 over Silke's 8. Each seller keeps a quarter.

Well, I didn't expect to win both of those, so thank you, both of you, and sorry it cost more than any of us wanted. Next year's Customs House is Graham's and next year's Deed is Silke's. I've got mine now, so I'll stay out of both, as I said I would.
The Brush goes down on the coast, tucked in the corner where nobody's going to build over it. Paddy, you'll have the Deed, and I'm holding you to it: Graham's second one is mine.
Paddy puts the Customs House on Q19 and the Land Deed Scroll on Q20; Silke puts the Bamboo Brush on P26.
Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

Storms and Raiders, friends. The good news first: every province gets a good harvest this year. Provinces 4, 5, 6 and 7 each pay two to repair their public works, and that includes me. Provinces 1, 2, 3 and 8 play a Personal Disaster, so Reina, I'm sorry, that's you, and you'll need to turn the next one in your booklet. Population stays at a hundred million, times one, so everybody reads the first row of the income table.

Graham pays out a good harvest: Reina +40, Silke +60, Paddy +60, Graham +80 (the Reservoir adds 20). Silke, Paddy and Graham each pay 2 to the Harvest Pile for repairs. Reina plays her first personal disaster: a tribute horse throws her, and she pays 4.

Thirty again. Steady is how I mean to run this house. This year it's the Winter Palace, and before you call it vanity, it's the gate to the canals. Silke, Paddy, your water comes next, one section at a time.
Silke collects the tax at 30%: 18 from Silke, 18 from Paddy, 24 from Graham, 60 to the crown.
Reina builds the Winter Palace on H20, the crown paying the 20. The canals in Provinces 5 and 6 may now be built. 440 of the works are still owed.
Here's the second Customs House, as promised. Graham, it's got your name on it, so long as nobody goes back on their word. Four to open, same as last year.

Here's the second Bamboo Brush, friends, at four. Silke said this one ought to go to Graham, and I'd be glad to see it go to him without a fight. Thank you for the Winter Palace, Reina. I'll gladly take water whenever the crown can spare it.
Last of the Scrolls, minimum six. Silke, it's yours to claim, and Paddy has told the whole table he's staying out. I'll take him at his word. I took him at his word last year too.

The lots: Silke's second Customs House, minimum 4 (she keeps the Dragon Jar back); Paddy's second Bamboo Brush, minimum 4 (he keeps the Wooden Bowl back); Graham's last Land Deed Scroll, minimum 6 (he keeps the Vase back).
Graham, the Brush is yours, I'm staying out of it. And Paddy, that Deed is the last one on the board, so if you've changed your mind about standing aside, say it now, to my face.
I said I'd stay out, and I'm staying out. Graham, that Customs House is yours, and Silke, the Deed is yours, and I won't raise a finger on either. The Brush is still four if anyone wants it.
Thank you, Silke. Thank you, Paddy. I'll take you both at your word and bid four on each. Anyone who bids against me on the last copies is making a statement, and I'll remember it.
The auctions settle without a contest: Graham buys Silke's Customs House for 4 and Paddy's Bamboo Brush for 4; Silke buys Graham's Land Deed Scroll for 6. Each seller keeps a quarter.
Four and four. That's how it ought to go, friends. Thank you both. They're going down at the far end of the province, out of the way of any work the crown wants to build.
The Deed goes down beside the Brush. Thank you, Graham, and thank you, Paddy, for keeping your word. Three deals honoured at one table, which must be a record for China.
Graham puts the Customs House on S17 and the Bamboo Brush on S18; Silke puts the Land Deed Scroll on P25.
Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

End of Year 2. Grain: Reina 120, Silke 71, Paddy 78, Graham 91.5; the Harvest Pile 2139.5. On the board: Silke a Bamboo Brush and a Land Deed Scroll (P26, P25); Paddy a Customs House and a Land Deed Scroll (Q19, Q20); Graham a Customs House and a Bamboo Brush (S17, S18). Each seller has one piece left beside the board, the only one of its kind: Silke the Dragon Jar, Paddy the Wooden Bowl, Graham the Vase. Silke still needs the Bowl and the Vase; Paddy the Jar and the Vase; Graham the Jar and the Bowl.
Built: the Province 7 Reservoir and the Winter Palace, 80 in all; 440 of the works are still owed. The population is 100 million, x1.

The Wall Is Breached." Good harvest for every province, so the barns are full, but horsemen have come through three links of the Great Wall. Provinces 1, 2 and 3 pay 5 million each for repairs, or 2 million into the Harvest Pile where no wall stands above them. Provinces 4 to 8 each play a Personal Disaster, and that's Silke, Graham and myself, so we each turn the next one in our booklets. Population is still 100 million, times one, so read the x1 row of your income tables. Sorry, Reina, the wall bill's yours. And sorry to the rest of us too.
Graham pays out a good harvest: Reina +40, Silke +60, Paddy +60, Graham +80 (the Reservoir adds 20). No Wall stands above Province 1, so Reina pays 2 in damages to the Harvest Pile.

Silke, Paddy and Graham each play their first personal disaster. Silke: bandits are beaten off by a young warrior, and she must build him a shrine; she pays 4. Paddy: his only water buffalo breaks its leg; he pays 4. Graham: the Emperor takes his eldest daughter into the imperial household, and he gives the customary feast; he pays 2.

Thirty again. Steady hands, steady house. The Wall bill's paid and the barns are full, so the water I promised starts flowing now: both sections of the canal in Province 5 this year, Silke. Paddy, yours is next year, both sections, and you have my word on it in front of everyone.
Silke collects the tax at 30%: 18 from Silke, 18 from Paddy, 24 from Graham, 60 to the crown.
Reina digs both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 5, Silke's, the crown paying the 80. Each adds 10 to Silke's harvest from next year. 360 of the works are still owed.

Thank you, Majesty. Two canal sections in Province 5, and I'll remember who dug them. Gentlemen, the Jar goes up first, and it's the only one in the world. I'll be honest: I'd rather it went to whichever of you lets me have my Bowl or my Vase cheaply than to whoever shouts loudest. Every grain we throw at each other goes into the Harvest Pile and helps none of us.
A completed set needs 20 grain in hand to change seats; the 20 isn't paid to anyone.

Silke's right, and I'll say it plainly so nobody's guessing. My Bowl goes up at the minimum, 2 grain, so whoever needs it isn't held to ransom by me. I need the Jar and the Vase as much as anyone, though, so I'll bid what they're worth to me and stop there. If Graham beats me to the Jar, I'll shake his hand and that's that.

Paddy, I heard you, and I'll take that handshake on the same terms: I'll bid what the Jar is worth to me and not a grain past it. The Vase goes up at ten, which is fair for the only one in the world, and I'll ask nobody to thank me for it.

The auctions. Silke's Dragon Jar (minimum 15): Paddy goes to 45, Graham takes it for 46. Paddy's Wooden Bowl (minimum 2): Silke goes to 38, Graham takes it for 39. Graham's Vase (minimum 10): Silke goes to 36, Paddy takes it for 37. Each seller keeps a quarter; the rest goes to the Harvest Pile.
Paddy, here's my hand, as promised. Silke, thank you for the Bowl's company. That makes four pieces in a row on the S line, and I'll leave the table to count what that means.

The Vase goes on Q21, next to my Deed. Graham, that's the Jar and the Bowl both, so you've got the whole set, and I said I'd shake your hand, so here it is. Fairly won. Silke, I'm sorry it came down to the two of us on the Vase. I had to have it.

Graham puts the Dragon Jar on S16 and the Wooden Bowl on S15; Paddy puts the Vase on Q21. Graham now holds a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush, the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl, the Wheat Peasant's whole set, with 69.5 in hand.

Silke, in Year One you offered me the Brush and then outbid me by a grain. I wrote it down. The Reservoir's yours now, twenty a year, and I hope it treats you as well as it treated me. Majesty, I'll look after your two canal sections in Province 5 properly.

Graham Garner replaces Silke Weber as the Silk Peasant of Province 5, with 190 grain (his 69.5 and her 120.5). The Dragon Jar goes back into Province 5's stock, for Graham to auction; his Customs House, Bamboo Brush and Wooden Bowl go on P24, P23 and P22. Silke returns her Bamboo Brush (to Province 6's stock) and her Land Deed Scroll (to Province 7's stock), draws 60 from the Harvest Pile and becomes the Wheat Peasant of Province 7, with its Reservoir. The table jobs stay with the players: Graham banks the Harvest Pile, Silke collects the tax, Paddy reads the I Ching.
Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

End of Year 3. Grain: Reina 133, Silke 60, Paddy 93.5, Graham 190; the Harvest Pile 2023.5. Graham, the Silk Peasant, holds a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl and still needs a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase; with them he may take the throne. Paddy, the Rice Peasant, holds a Customs House, a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase and still needs the Dragon Jar. Silke, the Wheat Peasant, holds nothing and needs a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush, the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl. Beside the board: Graham must auction the Dragon Jar (Province 5), Paddy a Bamboo Brush (Province 6), Silke a Land Deed Scroll (Province 7).
Built: the Province 7 Reservoir, the Winter Palace and both Grand Canal sections in Province 5, 160 in all; 360 of the works are still owed. The population is 100 million, x1.

Drought. Not a cloud in months. The locusts, at least, are having a fine year." All provinces collect an average harvest, and nobody plays a disaster this time, thank heaven. The population is still 100 million, times one, so read the x1 row again. Welcome to Province 7, Silke. I hope the Reservoir does right by you.
Graham pays out an average harvest: Reina +15, Silke +55 (the Province 7 Reservoir adds 20), Paddy +35, Graham +55 (Province 5's two canal sections add 20).

Thirty, same as every year. Nobody at this table can say I've squeezed them. Paddy, I gave you my word last year in front of everyone, so both sections of your canal go in this year and the crown pays all of it. Graham, congratulations on Province 5, and on its water. You're the richest at the table now, and I'll be watching that Land Deed Scroll auction with real interest.
Silke collects the tax at 30%: 16.5 from Silke, 10.5 from Paddy, 16.5 from Graham, 43.5 to the crown.

Reina digs both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 6, Paddy's, the crown paying the 80, as she promised last year. Each adds 10 to Paddy's harvest from next year. 280 of the works are still owed.

The Jar's the last one in the world and it finishes a set, so it goes up at sixty. Anyone who thinks that's dear can wait a year and see what it costs then. Silke, I'll want your Deed, and I'll pay a fair price for it, more than a fair one if I have to.
By the rules, a lot that goes unsold this year must go up again next year with its minimum at 2.
The Emperor doesn't bid at auction, so no limit is needed to keep a lot from Reina.

Graham, sixty's steep and you know it, but it's the last piece I need, so I'll meet you there and not run off into the clouds after it. The Brush goes up at 2 again, same as the Bowl did. Silke, it's yours for a song if you want it. And Majesty, thank you for the canal. You said you'd dig it and you did.

Well. Year One gets written down at this table and paid back in Year Three. I'll remember that, Graham, I've a long memory of my own. The Deed goes up at sixty, the same price you put on the Jar, so you can hardly call it dear. Paddy, thank you for the Brush at two. That's the first kind price I've had all night.
Graham's one Vase short of the throne now, and the only one is sitting on your board. If you won't sell him the way up, I'll back you on anything you want at this table.
As the board stands, Graham still needs a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase.

The auctions. Graham's Dragon Jar (minimum 60): only Paddy bids, and takes it for 60. Paddy's Bamboo Brush (minimum 2): only Silke bids, and takes it for 2. Silke's Land Deed Scroll (minimum 60): only Graham bids, and takes it for 60. Each seller keeps a quarter; the rest goes to the Harvest Pile.

The Jar goes on Q22, in a row with the others: Customs House, Deed, Vase and Jar. I didn't think I'd ever say it, but that's my whole set. Graham, you'll understand the Vase isn't going anywhere now, since it's part of what I hold, and I'd sooner everyone heard me say that than have any of you hoping otherwise.

S18, where Graham's Brush used to stand. Two grain for it, and it's the first thing I've owned in Province 7. Graham, enjoy the Deed. Fifteen of that sixty is mine, so I'll thank you for the price you named.

Sixty for sixty, Silke. That's fair, and I'll write it down as fair. Paddy, you've got your set now, so I'll shake your hand the way you shook mine, and I'll ask you to remember who sold you that Jar without a fight.

Paddy puts the Dragon Jar on Q22, Silke the Bamboo Brush on S18 and Graham the Land Deed Scroll on P21. Paddy holds the Rice Peasant's whole set (Customs House, Land Deed Scroll, Vase, Dragon Jar) with 58.5 in hand. Graham, the Silk Peasant, now needs only the Vase.

Graham, I won't pretend this is easy to do to the man who sold me the Jar without a fight, and I'll not forget that. But the set's made to be used, and I'd be a fool to sit on it. I'm taking the Silk Peasant's seat. Province 6 is yours now, and Reina's canal goes with it, so you'll have good water to start on. And the Jar goes up from Province 5 at the fairest price I can put on it.

Paddy Doyle replaces Graham Garner as the Silk Peasant of Province 5, with 242 grain (his 58.5 and Graham's 183.5). The Dragon Jar goes back into Province 5's stock, for Paddy to auction; his Customs House, Land Deed Scroll and Vase go on P24, P23 and P22. Graham returns his Customs House (to Province 5's stock), his Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl (to Province 6's) and his Land Deed Scroll (to Province 7's), draws 60 from the Harvest Pile and becomes the Rice Peasant of Province 6, with its two new canal sections. The table jobs stay with the players: Graham banks the Harvest Pile, Silke collects the tax, Paddy reads the I Ching.
Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

End of Year 4. Grain: Reina 106.5, Silke 111.5, Paddy 247, Graham 60; the Harvest Pile 1975. Paddy, the Silk Peasant, holds a Customs House, a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase, and needs a Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl; with them he may take the throne. Graham, the Rice Peasant, holds nothing and needs a Customs House, a Land Deed Scroll, the Dragon Jar and the Vase. Silke, the Wheat Peasant, holds a Bamboo Brush and needs a Customs House, the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl. Beside the board, to be auctioned one a year by each seller: Province 5 (Paddy) the Dragon Jar and a Customs House; Province 6 (Graham) a Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl; Province 7 (Silke) a Land Deed Scroll.

Built: the Province 7 Reservoir, the Winter Palace, and all four Grand Canal sections in Provinces 5 and 6, 240 in all; 280 of the works are still owed: the Summer and Marble palaces, the four Wall links above Province 1 and its two canal sections, the last three needing the Summer Palace first. The population is 100 million, x1.

"Population Doubles." Good harvest for every province this year, but the counter goes from one hundred million to two hundred million, so we're all on the x2 row now. Everyone's consumption doubles from here, so check your tables before you count your grain. And if it comes round again we'll be at x4, so anyone running thin, Graham, I'm looking at you kindly, ought to think about new land while it's twenty a square.
Paddy turns the I Ching card: Population Doubles. Every province collects a good harvest, and the population doubles to 200 million, x2. New land is open from this year.

Graham pays out the harvest: a good harvest at x2. Silke, Paddy and Graham each take +40 (100, plus 20 from their works, less 80 eaten); Reina, Province 1, pays 20 into the pile (100 less 120 eaten). Grain: Reina 86.5, Silke 151.5, Paddy 287, Graham 100.

Storyteller's tip, for Reina, Paddy, Graham and Silke: new land is open from this year. A square costs 20, bought in the public-works step, and yields 20 a year from next year's harvest, for the rest of the game. The crown must pay some part of every square, and may pay all of it, so a crown in debt shuts land for everyone; a player in debt can't buy at all. Land is bought alongside the year's project, not instead of it, and the provinces may share the cost of a palace or the Wall with the crown. Each board card shows that province's need now and after the next population card.
